material_findings: MANTA Table 2 isolates task-conditioned initial topology planning as -14.2pp success when removed and topology mutation as -10.9pp when removed in its four-benchmark 30-task-per-benchmark ablation.

MANTA constrains structural self-modification: max 5 initial agents, max 10 after repair, and <=3 operations per mutation; its progressive mutation-budget study reports the first repair opportunity provides the largest average gain and later repairs have diminishing returns.

MANTA structural playbook transfer reports +3.3pp mean in-domain and +3.3pp mean cross-domain gain at mutation budget zero in the tested PlanCraft/WorkBench setup, while compared adaptive baselines are neutral or negative cross-domain.

MANTA is token-efficient relative to tested multi-agent/workflow baselines but remains much more expensive than the single-agent baseline; no matched-token mutation ablation was found, so repair quality and extra compute are not fully separated.
The currently exposed official MANTA Hugging Face repository did not provide executable author code in this run, so quantitative claims remain paper-reported rather than independently reproduced.
